This is a draft based on how the website currently operates (as of October 19, 2026). It is not the official policy and has not been reviewed by an attorney. Excerpts in [brackets] need to be confirmed. The "Points for the attorney" section at the end summarizes everything that requires special attention.

The website "Idiomas com Prof. Brune" offers language lessons and personalized guidance from a teacher. Data controller: [CONFIRM: full name or business name and CNPJ or CPF]. Privacy contact: [CONFIRM: email].
Account: email, display name, username (@), password (stored securely by the login service), website language, account type (user, teacher, or administrator), and plan (Free or Premium).
Profile (optional): photo, bio, country, gender, featured badge, and whether the profile is public or private.

Study: completed lessons, flashcards and each one's memory schedule (when to review it again), points (XP), days studied, day streak, achievements, decks and your own flashcards, and the images and audio you upload to the flashcards.
Social features on the site: friendships and invitations, nudges, congratulations, duo missions, ranking position and, on the Mural, the posts and files you upload.
Website usage: pages viewed and actions taken, device type, browser, operating system, and a session identifier. We use this information to improve the website and understand what works.
Notifications: preferences, website bell notifications, devices registered for push notifications, and emails sent by the website (for example, account confirmation).
Support requests (Reports): the text you write, an optional screenshot, the device's technical specifications, and your email address, if you ask for a reply.
Card audio: when you generate a card's voice recording, the card's text is sent to the voice service, and a record of who requested it is stored to track the monthly quota.
2.2 If you are linked to a teacher
The link itself (start date, language, and whether it is active).
The lessons she records for you: date, attendance, skills, materials, and comments. You cannot see her private notes.

The flashcards she creates for you, including those generated from your lesson notes, and your answers to them: whether you got them right or wrong, when, whether it was in class or at home, and whether you typed the answer.
Support materials she sends and posts on her Mural.
Classes: if the teacher places you in a class, she and the other members follow whatever belongs to the class. [CONFIRM: what classmates see]
Your account information and account type (granted by the administrator).
The list of linked students and what they allow you to see: study progress and their answers to the flashcards you created.
What you write on the website: lessons (with private notes), flashcards, support materials, the Mural, invitation codes, and the calendar link.

Calendar: the calendar link (.ics) shows lesson times and students' names. Anyone with the link can see the calendar, so the link is secret and can be replaced. Private notes and comments never appear in it.
Review Bank: items extracted from your lesson notebooks, including from people who do not have an account yet (see 2.4).

You are responsible for what you write down about students and should record only what is necessary for teaching. [CONFIRM with the lawyer: roles of controller and processor between the administrator and the teacher]
2.4 People who do not have an account yet

The teacher can store in the Review Bank the name of people who have not yet created an account, items taken from lessons (words, phrases, and mistakes), and the answers given in class. These people have not yet received this policy. [CONFIRM: legal basis and how to inform these people]

When you have an active connection with a teacher, she can see your study progress on the website, the flashcards she has prepared for you, and your answers to those flashcards: which ones you got right or wrong, when you studied, and whether you studied in class or at home. She cannot see your password or any of your other private information. Private notes that the teacher writes about the lessons are not visible to you.

The teacher uses this information to decide what to review in class and what homework to assign. When the connection ends, she can no longer see your new answers. [CONFIRM: what part of your history she continues to see after the connection ends]

The teacher writes down the lesson content in her own documents (Google Docs). An artificial intelligence tool reads these documents and her calendar every night to extract words, phrases, and mistakes and turn them into review flashcards. These notes may mention personal matters discussed during the conversation. Items containing personal or sensitive information are not automatically turned into flashcards: they are set aside for the teacher to decide. [CONFIRM: name of the tool provider, whether the data is used to train models, and how long the provider keeps the content]

Other people on the site: your name, @ handle, points, and achievements appear in the leaderboard and in Friends depending on your profile settings. A private profile hides your photo, bio, progress, and decks from anyone who isn't your friend or your teacher.

Services that help us run the website: Supabase (database, login, and files; servers in Brazil [CONFIRM: region]), Resend (email delivery), Google Cloud Text-to-Speech (voice for the flashcards; receives only the card text), GitHub Pages (website hosting), and browsers' push notification delivery services.
Third-party libraries and fonts (Google Fonts, cdnjs, and jsDelivr): when you open the website, your browser contacts these services, and they receive your network address (IP address).
We do not sell your data, and we do not use it for third-party advertising. [CONFIRM]

To create and maintain your account, show your progress, schedule your reviews, allow your teacher to follow your progress, send notifications that you have enabled, respond to requests for help, keep the website secure, and improve teaching. [CONFIRM with the lawyer: the legal basis for each purpose under the LGPD (consent, performance of a contract, legitimate interest)]
7. How long we keep your data

Currently, the website does not delete data automatically and does not have a button to delete an account: data remains as long as the account exists, and deletion is done upon request. If you ask, we will delete or anonymize your data, except for what the law requires us to keep. [CONFIRM: retention periods by data type and whether we will create a "Delete account" button]

Under the LGPD, you may request: confirmation that we process your data, access to your data, correction, anonymization or deletion, data portability, information about who we share your data with, and the revocation of consent. Please email [CONFIRM: email]. You can also adjust your public or private profile and notifications in Settings.
[CONFIRM: minimum age for use and how we handle minors, including consent from guardians]
If we change this policy, we will post a notice on the website. The version date is listed at the top. [CONFIRM: date and version]

How to ask for someone's data and how to handle a request

What we ask for when you sign up: email, password, display name, and username. Everything else (photo, country, gender, bio) is optional, and you choose whether it is shown to other people. [CONFIRM: exact sign-up fields]

Data about a student that the teacher writes down (lessons, flashcards, mistakes) comes from the teacher, not from the student. That is why the policy needs to say this clearly and inform the student.

Currently, there is no button for a person to view or download their own data or to delete their account. The request arrives by email [CONFIRM: address]; the administrator confirms the person's identity through the account email, gathers the data from the tables listed in the map, and replies. [CONFIRM with the lawyer: LGPD deadlines for the reply]

Currently, the website does not charge anything and does not store card or bank account data. When the Premium plan is billed through Stripe, the payment happens on Stripe's secure page: the card number and bank details go directly to Stripe and never pass through our database. We will store only the customer and subscription identifiers, the plan, the status, and the dates. Stripe stores payment data according to its own rules. [CONFIRM: Stripe's role (controller or processor), country of storage, retention of invoices, cancellation and refunds in the Terms]
